title: Frozen worked example — six-language parity anchor for authenticated invocation (RFC 001 §5.1)
description: This vector is the single source of truth for cross-SDK authenticated-invocation parity. It pins the DESCRIPTOR-BOUND canonical invocation bytes — the admission/proof boundary. `ability` is an AbilityDescriptorRef (`ability_ura@version#descriptor_hash!action`) and `subject` is normalized to an EntityRef inside the canonical encoding. Every SDK's worked-example test MUST load this file, run its descriptor-bound encoder/signer (canonical_descriptor_bound_invocation_bytes + sign_descriptor_bound_invocation), and assert against these values. Retired plain invocation bytes are NOT the proof boundary and are not pinned here. No SDK is permitted to hard-code these values in test code. Any change that alters `expected` values is a spec change — stop, amend the RFC, regenerate from the Rust reference (`sdk/rust/examples/emit_worked_example.rs`), update this file, update AUTHENTICATED_INVOCATION.md §4.1.3, commit all three together.

metadata_excluded.description: Adding arbitrary non-axiom metadata MUST NOT change canonical_invocation_sha256. Conformant SDKs produce byte-identical canonical bytes for the envelope above regardless of any metadata attached at transport level.

nonce_not_generated_from_time_or_uuid.description: When a test generates its own nonce (for fresh calls unrelated to this vector), it MUST use the SDK's fresh_nonce / freshNonce CSPRNG wrapper. Using time, UUID, counter, or hash is prohibited and MUST be caught by code review / grep.

seed_pubkey_binding.description: expected.caller_pubkey_hex is the pure Ed25519 derivation of inputs.signing_seed_hex per RFC 8032 §5.1.5. Divergence here means the SDK's Ed25519 library is wrong, not that this file drifted.

consumers.loader_rule: Each SDK test MUST load this JSON file (path resolution walks up from current dir to find sdk/conformance/cases/axiom/). Tests MUST NOT hard-code the inputs or expected values; the JSON is the ONLY source of truth.
